answer: At dawn, a verifier assigns each peer a quartz-timestamped micro-benchmark: solve 2^22 hash iterations and post the result before a 90-second wall-clock deadline. Clones sharing one GPU fall into a canyon of staggered completions, since concurrent launches split FLOPS and blow the deadline by 40-plus seconds, each failed round burning roughly $0.30 of rented compute. Peers who miss two deadlines get their identity weight zeroed and must re-stake $500 before re-entry, so spinning up 10,000 sockpuppets costs about $3,000,000 to buy one vote.
